Then I set up three CUDA streams — one for interior compute, one for boundary compute, and one for communication — and start sketching the iteration loop: pack boundary values on the comm stream, copy them to host, then launch interior compute concurrently while the exchange proceeds.\n\nFor the overlap sequence I'm working through synchronization carefully: waiting on the comm stream before posting MPI sends, confirming any prior host-to-device ghost copy is finished before letting MPI overwrite the receive buffer, then issuing Isend/Irecv, copying received ghosts back to device, and using a stream-wait event so the boundary kernel only fires once ghosts are ready. I verify that interior and boundary kernels write disjoint regions of the \"next\" buffer so there's no race, before finally synchronizing all three streams and swapping buffers for the next iteration.\n\nI need to handle timing carefully: barrier before and after the loop, syncing the device, using the same clock as before. Initialization should zero out device arrays and use pinned host buffers. I also need to guard against ranks with zero owned elements when process count exceeds element count—skip kernel launches in that case but still allocate at least one element so cudaMalloc/cudaMallocHost calls don't fail on zero size.\n\nFor the neighbor exchange, I'll just use a fixed tag since each pair exchanges exactly once per iteration and MPI_Waitall guarantees completion before the next round. I'm setting up MPI_Alltoall to exchange ghost counts and MPI_Alltoallv with 64-bit indices to exchange the actual global indices, since N can exceed 32-bit range even though per-rank counts fit in int. Ghosts are kept sorted by global index so each owner's ghost entries stay contiguous, letting me compute per-owner offsets and counts with a simple scan.\n\nThe direction of the Alltoall is a bit subtle: what I store as \"what I want to receive from q\" becomes, after the exchange, \"what q needs to send to me,\" so I need to be careful mapping recv_count to send_count correctly across ranks. Then I use Alltoallv to actually exchange the index requests, with sdispls/rdispls built from prefix sums, converting received global indices into local offsets for sending back data. Finally I build the neighbor list by checking which ranks have nonzero send or receive counts, though looping over all P ranks each iteration could become a bottleneck at scale.\n\nI'm now setting up the nonblocking Isend/Irecv pairs per neighbor for the halo exchange, which should avoid deadlock since everything is asynchronous. At the end, I gather the owned elements from each rank into a host buffer and use Gatherv on rank 0 to assemble the full array, with recvcounts and displs scaled by the element size, and I confirm the struct layout has no padding so the byte math lines up cleanly.\n\nI'm adjusting validateResults and computeHash to operate on a plain vector of ElementDynamic rather than the World struct, keeping the same printing logic for energy data and memory usage. I also need to make sure argument parsing, error handling, and help output are consistent across all ranks, with printing restricted to rank 0, and MPI_Finalize called properly before any early return so all ranks exit cleanly together.\n\nTo keep exit codes consistent across ranks, I'll broadcast the return code computed by root after validation, finalize MPI, and then return that same code everywhere. I'm also adding a check for invalid grid sizes (n < 1) that prints an error on root only but still returns consistently across ranks, while negative iteration counts remain a no-op since the loop condition already handles that safely.\n\nNow I'm setting up GPU device detection and selecting a CUDA device per node, splitting the MPI communicator by shared memory type so each process can map to a distinct GPU.\n\nI'm deciding to keep the printed output format identical to the original rather than adding new informational lines, since the results parsing relies on consistent output structure. Now I'm turning to the update kernel's memory access pattern, making sure connectivity and field loads stay coalesced across threads for performance.\n\nWriting update kernel...\n\nI'm also double-checking the connected flux read, the packing kernel that gathers values by index, and that the ghost indices stay within the extended array bounds. The host-side CUDA setup creates non-blocking streams for overlap.\n\nNow I'm designing a Partition struct that computes rank boundaries across N elements split among P ranks, with an owner lookup using binary search over the start offsets to handle uneven remainders and empty ranks correctly.\n\nI'm also defining the material set (three materials with their emissivity/reflectivity values) and building per-element static data—determining each element's material index and its connected neighbors (up to 4, based on grid position) with flux values of 1.0.\n\nI realize I need signed coordinates to avoid underflow issues when checking boundary neighbors, so I'll switch to int64_t for the x/y grid indices. Now I'm sketching the LocalMesh structure that each rank will hold: owned/ghost element ranges, SoA arrays for connection counts, materials, connectivity, flux values, and interior/boundary/ghost element lists.\n\nI'm building out the ghost discovery logic — each thread scans owned elements' connections in parallel, collecting any neighbor indices outside the local range as ghost candidates, then merges them safely across threads.\n\nAfter deduplicating the ghost list with sort and unique, I'm computing the local index mapping in parallel: for each owned element, storing its connection count, material index, and mapping each neighbor to either its local owned slot or a ghost slot found via binary search into the sorted ghost array.\n\nI'm reconsidering the padded array layout for connections—using a fixed stride of MAX_CONN slots per element wastes memory even though reads stay efficient, so I'm switching to a stride based on the actual maximum connection count observed, which for a square grid works out to 4 slots instead of 8.\n\nI need to handle the edge case where that max could be zero for isolated elements, guarding allocation sizes accordingly. Then I'm working through boundary classification (flagging elements with ghost neighbors), building the per-owner ghost send/receive counts, and assembling the concatenated send buffer for the Alltoallv exchange.\n\nOnce the data is laid out, I'm planning the device-side upload: connectivity arrays, material flags, flux buffers, interior/boundary index lists, and pinned host buffers for the send/receive communication, all sized by n_owned, n_total, n_send, and n_ghost.\n\nI'm defining small helper templates for allocating device memory and uploading host vectors, then setting up the double-buffered E and F field arrays for the timed iteration loop, where halo receives are posted first for each neighbor so the GPU can keep working while the exchange completes.\n\nFor each step: pack outgoing boundary data on the comm stream and copy it to host, launch the interior update concurrently on a separate stream, then sync the comm stream before sending/waiting on MPI, finally upload the received halo and trigger the boundary update once an event confirms the ghost data has landed.\n\nI verify there's no data race between the H2D ghost copy and the interior kernel since they touch disjoint regions, confirm the event ordering is correct, and note that requests and tags need to be reset each iteration; also flagging that MPI calls from the host thread alongside async CUDA kernels should work fine, though multithreaded MPI_Init needs checking.\n\nI'm using MPI_THREAD_FUNNELED since only the master thread issues MPI calls, with a check on the provided thread level. For timing, I'm wrapping the main loop with barriers and a device sync before measuring elapsed time, then copying the final owned state back to host after the loop completes.\n\nFor gathering results, I'm using MPI_Gatherv to collect each rank's owned elements into the root's full array, handling the empty-vector edge case safely, and keeping the gather outside the timed region. The final reporting, hashing, and result validation stay identical to the original logic, with only the root printing output.\n\nI'm computing CUDA kernel launch dimensions, syncing the communication stream after packing and copying data back to host, and cleaning up device memory, streams, and pinned buffers before calling MPI_Finalize. For the build setup, I'm writing the CMake configuration to require C++20/CUDA 20 standards, locate MPI, OpenMP, and the CUDA toolkit, and set up the executable target with appropriate architecture defaults.\n\nI'm working through compiler flag compatibility issues—specifically how to pass host-only flags like -march=native through nvcc using -Xcompiler, and whether optimization flags like -O3 apply correctly to both host and device code. I'm also weighing whether to avoid nvcc entirely for the kernel file, but conclude it's necessary since the CUDA launch syntax requires it, then checking GCC version compatibility with CUDA 12.0.\n\nI also realize OpenMP flags need special handling for CUDA sources—since linking against OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX normally passes -fopenmp directly, which nvcc will reject, so I need to manually prefix it with -Xcompiler instead.\n\nSimilarly, MPI's compile flags might include -pthread, which would also need -Xcompiler wrapping for CUDA files—I should check mpicxx's actual flags before assuming. For memory layout, I'll size E arrays for n_total (including ghosts) but F arrays only for n_owned since F is never read for ghost cells, keeping kernel indexing straightforward and saving memory. Now I'm moving to writing the host-side OpenMP interleaving code, handling the iteration counter type and command-line options.\n\nFor numerical correctness, since the host never computes per-element arithmetic directly and all device computation uses the same left-to-right evaluation order as the original (difference times transfer coefficient times flux times 0.25), the results should be bit-identical and verifiable via diff. I also need to check the single-process case where there are no ghosts or boundary elements at all, so the boundary kernel launch is skipped entirely while the interior kernel handles everything — the event synchronization still needs to work correctly in that degenerate case.\n\nNow I'm starting to write the actual MPI/CUDA source file, setting up includes for MPI, OpenMP, and CUDA runtime, along with standard library headers and the results output helper. I'm defining basic types and constants, then beginning the data structures for materials and elements.\n\nStill writing structures...\n\nI'm now implementing buildLocalMesh, which computes each rank's owned element range from the partition and builds static connectivity data for them in parallel, being careful to use a signed loop type for OpenMP compatibility.\n\nNext I'm identifying ghost elements by scanning each owned element's connections in parallel, collecting any indices that fall outside the local range, then merging and deduplicating them across threads. From there I'm sizing the local mesh structures, computing the maximum connection count per element to size the slots, and beginning to allocate the per-element arrays for connection counts, materials, and connectivity.\n\nThen I'm filling in each element's material index and connection list, mapping ghost indices to their local slot positions via binary search into the sorted ghost array, and storing the corresponding flux values alongside. After that I'm splitting elements into interior and boundary groups based on whether any neighbor is a ghost, setting up material property tables, and starting to build the communication pattern by counting how many ghosts belong to each remote partition.\n\nNow I'm setting up the all-to-all exchange: swapping counts between ranks, computing displacement offsets, then exchanging the actual requested global indices so each owning rank learns which of its local elements are needed elsewhere. From there I translate those requested indices into local offsets for the send buffer and build the final neighbor list from ranks with nonzero send or receive counts.\n\nWith the partition and communication pattern built identically on every rank, I'm now sketching the main function: initializing MPI with threading support, parsing arguments consistently across ranks, validating the grid size, printing the header on the root rank, and moving into device selection before mesh construction begins.\n\nEach rank picks its GPU by splitting the communicator by shared-memory node and assigning devices round-robin based on local rank, with a fatal error if no CUDA devices are found. Then I build the mesh locally per rank, have root print memory usage estimates, and start defining the device-side buffer struct holding fields, connectivity, materials, and flux arrays for the simulation.\n\nI'm structuring the GPU simulation loop with MPI barriers around timing so root measures elapsed computation time accurately, then after the run I gather each rank's owned dynamic state into a full array on root using counts and displacements for an MPI gather.\n\nI'm also adding cleanup for GPU resources, abort handling on fatal CUDA errors, and small helper utilities for launching kernels with the right block/grid dimensions and nonblocking streams.\n\nNow I'm writing the main simulation loop: it alternates between buffer pairs each iteration, sets up nonblocking receives for halo data from neighboring ranks into pinned memory, and copies received ghost values into device buffers before computing the next timestep.\n\nAfter the ghost H2D copy completes, I record an event and have the boundary stream wait on it before running the boundary update kernel, then sync all three streams before swapping buffers. {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793099347477,"sessionID":"ses_e82f8d758ffepCNsAzGL5Mftpd","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01VaUTeoTyTmHFiT2cCvAzAw","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/unstructured_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r4/unstructured/unstructured.cpp","content":"// Unstructured mesh energy transfer benchmark.\n//\n// Parallelization (all three are always used):\n//   MPI    - the element index space is block-partitioned across ranks. Each rank owns a\n//            contiguous range of elements and keeps ghost copies of the remote neighbours\n//            it reads. Halo exchange uses nonblocking point-to-point messages that only\n//            involve ranks that actually share connectivity.\n//   CUDA   - each rank drives one GPU (node-local rank modulo device count). The element\n//            update is a CUDA kernel. Interior elements (no ghost neighbours) are updated\n//            concurrently with the halo exchange; boundary elements are updated once the\n//            halo has arrived.\n//   OpenMP - host-side setup (mesh construction, ghost discovery, index remapping) and the\n//            final state unpacking run as OpenMP parallel loops.\n//\n// The per-element arithmetic keeps the original evaluation order, and the device code uses\n// non-contracting intrinsics, so results are bit-identical to the serial reference.\n\n#include <mpi.h>\n#include <omp.h>\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <climits>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdint>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <limits>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n// Types to represent unstructured mesh elements\nusing idx_t = uint64_t;\nusing val_t = double;\n\n// Maximum number of connections per element (for a 2D grid: 4 neighbors)\nconstexpr int MAX_CONNECTIONS = 8;\n\n// Material properties for energy transfer\nstruct Material {\n    val_t transfer_coeff;  // Energy transfer coefficient\n    val_t external_flow;   // External energy source/sink\n};\n\n// Static connectivity information for each element\nstruct ElementStatic {\n    idx_t material_idx;\n    idx_t num_connections;\n    idx_t connected_idx[MAX_CONNECTIONS];     // Indices of connected elements\n    val_t connected_flux[MAX_CONNECTIONS];    // Flux coefficients for each connection\n};\n\n// Dynamic state for each element\nstruct ElementDynamic {\n    val_t current_energy;\n    val_t total_flux;\n};\nstatic_assert(sizeof(ElementDynamic) == 2 * sizeof(double), \"ElementDynamic must be two doubles\");\n\n// Material type IDs\nconstexpr idx_t DEFAULT_MAT_ID = 0;\nconstexpr idx_t INFLOW_MAT_ID = 1;\nconstexpr idx_t OUTFLOW_MAT_ID = 2;\n\nconstexpr int kBlockSize = 256;\nconstexpr int kHaloTag = 17;\n\n#define CHECK_CUDA(call)                                                          \\\n    do {                                                                          \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                                \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,      \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                    \\\n            MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);                                         \\\n        }                                                                         \\\n    } while (0)\n\n[[noreturn]] static void fatal(const char* msg) {\n    fprintf(stderr, \"Error: %s\\n\", msg);\n    MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);\n    std::abort();\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Mesh description\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nstd::vector<Material> makeMaterials() {\n    return {Material{0.8, 0.0}, Material{0.8, 0.5}, Material{0.8, -0.5}};\n}\n\n// Material of global element g of an n x n grid. Corner assignments are applied in the\n// same order as the original serial builder, so later assignments win.\nidx_t materialOf(idx_t g, idx_t n) {\n    const idx_t last = n - 1;\n    idx_t mat = DEFAULT_MAT_ID;\n    if (g == 0) mat = INFLOW_MAT_ID;                  // (0, 0)\n    if (g == last) mat = OUTFLOW_MAT_ID;              // (0, last)\n    if (g == last * n) mat = OUTFLOW_MAT_ID;          // (last, 0)\n    if (g == last * n + last) mat = INFLOW_MAT_ID;    // (last, last)\n    return mat;\n}\n\n// Static description of global element g: 4-neighbour connectivity on a 2D grid,\n// neighbours listed in the order (+x, -x, +y, -y), each with unit flux coefficient.\nElementStatic buildElementStatic(idx_t g, idx_t n_root) {\n    ElementStatic e{};\n    e.material_idx = materialOf(g, n_root);\n    e.num_connections = 0;\n\n    const int64_t n = static_cast<int64_t>(n_root);\n    const int64_t x = static_cast<int64_t>(g / n_root);\n    const int64_t y = static_cast<int64_t>(g % n_root);\n    constexpr int offsets[4][2] = {{1, 0}, {-1, 0}, {0, 1}, {0, -1}};\n    for (const auto& off : offsets) {\n        const int64_t nx = x + off[0];\n        const int64_t ny = y + off[1];\n        if (nx >= 0 && nx < n && ny >= 0 && ny < n) {\n            e.connected_idx[e.num_connections] = static_cast<idx_t>(nx * n + ny);\n            e.connected_flux[e.num_connections] = 1.0;\n            e.num_connections++;\n        }\n    }\n    return e;\n}\n\n// Contiguous block partition of [0, N) over P ranks. Rank r owns [start[r], start[r+1]).\nstruct Partition {\n    std::vector<idx_t> start;  // size P+1\n\n    int owner(idx_t g) const {\n        return static_cast<int>(std::upper_bound(start.begin(), start.end(), g) - start.begin()) - 1;\n    }\n};\n\nPartition makePartition(idx_t N, int P) {\n    Partition part;\n    part.start.resize(static_cast<size_t>(P) + 1);\n    const idx_t base = N / static_cast<idx_t>(P);\n    const idx_t rem = N % static_cast<idx_t>(P);\n    for (int r = 0; r <= P; ++r) {\n        part.start[r] = static_cast<idx_t>(r) * base + std::min<idx_t>(static_cast<idx_t>(r), rem);\n    }\n    return part;\n}\n\n// Per-rank view of the mesh. Local element ids: [0, n_owned) owned, [n_owned, n_owned + n_ghost) ghost.\nstruct LocalMesh {\n    idx_t begin = 0;\n    idx_t end = 0;\n    uint32_t n_owned = 0;\n    uint32_t n_ghost = 0;\n    uint32_t n_slots = 0;               // max connections over owned elements\n    std::vector<uint8_t> nconn;         // [i]\n    std::vector<uint8_t> mat;           // [i]\n    std::vector<uint32_t> conn;         // [slot * n_owned + i] local index of neighbour\n    std::vector<double> cflux;          // [slot * n_owned + i] connection flux coefficient\n    std::vector<uint32_t> interior;     // owned elements with no ghost neighbour\n    std::vector<uint32_t> boundary;     // owned elements with at least one ghost neighbour\n    std::vector<double> mat_tc;         // per material transfer coefficient\n    std::vector<double> mat_ext;        // per material external flow\n\n    // Communication pattern (indexed by rank)\n    std::vector<int> nbrs;              // ranks with traffic in either direction\n    std::vector<int> send_count, recv_count;\n    std::vector<int> send_off, recv_off;\n    std::vector<uint32_t> send_local;   // owned local ids to send, grouped by destination rank\n};\n\n// Builds this rank's portion of the mesh: owned static data, ghost discovery,\n// local index remapping, interior/boundary split, and the halo communication pattern.\nLocalMesh buildLocalMesh(idx_t n_root, const Partition& part, int rank, int nranks,\n                         const std::vector<Material>& mats, MPI_Comm comm) {\n    LocalMesh m;\n    m.begin = part.start[rank];\n    m.end = part.start[rank + 1];\n    const long long n_own = static_cast<long long>(m.end - m.begin);\n    if (n_own > static_cast<long long>(UINT32_MAX)) fatal(\"too many elements per rank\");\n    m.n_owned = static_cast<uint32_t>(n_own);\n\n    // 1. Static description of owned elements (global connectivity).\n    std::vector<ElementStatic> own(static_cast<size_t>(n_own));\n    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (long long i = 0; i < n_own; ++i) {\n        own[i] = buildElementStatic(m.begin + static_cast<idx_t>(i), n_root);\n    }\n\n    // 2. Ghost discovery: remote neighbours of owned elements, sorted and unique.\n    //    Sorted order groups ghosts by owning rank, so each owner's ghosts are contiguous.\n    std::vector<idx_t> ghosts;\n    #pragma omp parallel\n    {\n        std::vector<idx_t> found;\n        #pragma omp for schedule(static) nowait\n        for (long long i = 0; i < n_own; ++i) {\n            for (idx_t j = 0; j < own[i].num_connections; ++j) {\n                const idx_t g = own[i].connected_idx[j];\n                if (g < m.begin || g >= m.end) found.push_back(g);\n            }\n        }\n        #pragma omp critical\n        ghosts.insert(ghosts.end(), found.begin(), found.end());\n    }\n    std::sort(ghosts.begin(), ghosts.end());\n    ghosts.erase(std::unique(ghosts.begin(), ghosts.end()), ghosts.end());\n\n    if (static_cast<unsigned long long>(n_own) + ghosts.size() > UINT32_MAX) {\n        fatal(\"too many local elements (including ghosts) per rank\");\n    }\n    m.n_ghost = static_cast<uint32_t>(ghosts.size());\n\n    // 3. Local connectivity in structure-of-arrays layout, remapped to local ids.\n    uint32_t n_slots = 0;\n    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(static) reduction(max : n_slots)\n    for (long long i = 0; i < n_own; ++i) {\n        n_slots = std::max(n_slots, static_cast<uint32_t>(own[i].num_connections));\n    }\n    m.n_slots = n_slots;\n    const size_t nown = m.n_owned;\n    m.nconn.resize(nown);\n    m.mat.resize(nown);\n    m.conn.assign(static_cast<size_t>(n_slots) * nown, 0);\n    m.cflux.assign(static_cast<size_t>(n_slots) * nown, 0.0);\n\n    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (long long i = 0; i < n_own; ++i) {\n        const ElementStatic& e = own[i];\n        m.nconn[i] = static_cast<uint8_t>(e.num_connections);\n        m.mat[i] = static_cast<uint8_t>(e.material_idx);\n        for (idx_t j = 0; j < e.num_connections; ++j) {\n            const idx_t g = e.connected_idx[j];\n            uint32_t loc;\n            if (g >= m.begin && g < m.end) {\n                loc = static_cast<uint32_t>(g - m.begin);\n            } else {\n                const auto it = std::lower_bound(ghosts.begin(), ghosts.end(), g);\n                loc = m.n_owned + static_cast<uint32_t>(it - ghosts.begin());\n            }\n            const size_t slot = static_cast<size_t>(j) * nown + static_cast<size_t>(i);\n            m.conn[slot] = loc;\n            m.cflux[slot] = e.connected_flux[j];\n        }\n    }\n\n    // 4. Interior / boundary split (boundary elements read ghost values).\n    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < m.n_owned; ++i) {\n        bool touches_ghost = false;\n        for (uint32_t j = 0; j < m.nconn[i]; ++j) {\n            if (m.conn[static_cast<size_t>(j) * nown + i] >= m.n_owned) touches_ghost = true;\n        }\n        (touches_ghost ? m.boundary : m.interior).push_back(i);\n    }\n\n    m.mat_tc.resize(mats.size());\n    m.mat_ext.resize(mats.size());\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < mats.size(); ++k) {\n        m.mat_tc[k] = mats[k].transfer_coeff;\n        m.mat_ext[k] = mats[k].external_flow;\n    }\n\n    // 5. Halo communication pattern. Ghosts from rank p are requested from p; p learns\n    //    which of its elements to send by receiving the requested global indices.\n    const size_t P = static_cast<size_t>(nranks);\n    m.recv_count.assign(P, 0);\n    m.recv_off.assign(P, 0);\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < ghosts.size(); ++k) {\n        const int p = part.owner(ghosts[k]);\n        if (m.recv_count[p] == 0) m.recv_off[p] = static_cast<int>(k);\n        m.recv_count[p]++;\n    }\n\n    m.send_count.assign(P, 0);\n    CHECK_MPI_STATUS(MPI_Alltoall(m.recv_count.data(), 1, MPI_INT,\n                                  m.send_count.data(), 1, MPI_INT, comm));\n\n    std::vector<int> req_disp(P, 0);\n    int total_send = 0;\n    for (size_t p = 0; p < P; ++p) {\n        req_disp[p] = total_send;\n        total_send += m.send_count[p];\n    }\n    std::vector<idx_t> requested(static_cast<size_t>(total_send));\n    CHECK_MPI_STATUS(MPI_Alltoallv(ghosts.data(), m.recv_count.data(), m.recv_off.data(), MPI_UINT64_T,\n                                   requested.data(), m.send_count.data(), req_disp.data(), MPI_UINT64_T,\n                                   comm));\n\n    m.send_off = req_disp;\n    m.send_local.resize(requested.size());\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < requested.size(); ++k) {\n        const idx_t g = requested[k];\n        if (g < m.begin || g >= m.end) fatal(\"halo request for an element not owned by this rank\");\n        m.send_local[k] = static_cast<uint32_t>(g - m.begin);\n    }\n\n    for (int p = 0; p < nranks; ++p) {\n        if (p != rank && (m.send_count[p] > 0 || m.recv_count[p] > 0)) m.nbrs.push_back(p);\n    }\n    return m;\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// GPU kernels and device state\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n// Device view of the static mesh data.\nstruct MeshView {\n    uint32_t n_owned;\n    const uint8_t* nconn;\n    const uint8_t* mat;\n    const uint32_t* conn;\n    const double* cflux;\n    const double* mat_tc;\n    const double* mat_ext;\n};\n\n// Gather the energies that other ranks need into a contiguous send buffer.\n__global__ void packKernel(const double* __restrict__ E, const uint32_t* __restrict__ idx,\n                           double* __restrict__ out, uint32_t n) {\n    const uint32_t k = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (k < n) out[k] = E[idx[k]];\n}\n\n// One Jacobi-style update step for the listed owned elements.\n// Evaluation order matches the original computeFlux():\n//   total = ext; total += ((other - this) * tc * cf) * 0.25 over connections in order.\n// The __*_rn intrinsics prevent FMA contraction so results match the serial code.\n__global__ void updateKernel(MeshView mv, const uint32_t* __restrict__ list, uint32_t count,\n                             const double* __restrict__ E_in, const double* __restrict__ F_in,\n                             double* __restrict__ E_out, double* __restrict__ F_out) {\n    const uint32_t t = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (t >= count) return;\n    const uint32_t i = list[t];\n\n    const double e_self = E_in[i];\n    const uint32_t m = mv.mat[i];\n    const double tc = mv.mat_tc[m];\n    double total = mv.mat_ext[m];\n\n    const uint32_t nc = mv.nconn[i];\n    for (uint32_t j = 0; j < nc; ++j) {\n        const size_t slot = static_cast<size_t>(j) * mv.n_owned + i;\n        const double diff = __dsub_rn(E_in[mv.conn[slot]], e_self);\n        const double flux = __dmul_rn(__dmul_rn(__dmul_rn(diff, tc), mv.cflux[slot]), 0.25);\n        total = __dadd_rn(total, flux);\n    }\n\n    E_out[i] = __dadd_rn(e_self, total);\n    F_out[i] = __dadd_rn(F_in[i], fabs(total));\n}\n\nstruct GpuState {\n    cudaStream_t s_int = nullptr;\n    cudaStream_t s_bnd = nullptr;\n    cudaStream_t s_comm = nullptr;\n    cudaEvent_t ev_ghost = nullptr;\n\n    uint32_t n_owned = 0;\n    uint32_t n_ghost = 0;\n    uint32_t n_send = 0;\n    uint32_t n_int = 0;\n    uint32_t n_bnd = 0;\n\n    double* E[2] = {nullptr, nullptr};   // energy, double-buffered (owned + ghost slots)\n    double* F[2] = {nullptr, nullptr};   // total flux, double-buffered (owned only)\n    uint8_t* nconn = nullptr;\n    uint8_t* mat = nullptr;\n    uint32_t* conn = nullptr;\n    double* cflux = nullptr;\n    double* mat_tc = nullptr;\n    double* mat_ext = nullptr;\n    uint32_t* interior = nullptr;\n    uint32_t* boundary = nullptr;\n    uint32_t* send_idx = nullptr;\n    double* send_buf = nullptr;          // device staging for outgoing halo values\n    double* h_send = nullptr;            // pinned host staging, outgoing\n    double* h_recv = nullptr;            // pinned host staging, incoming ghosts\n    int cur = 0;                         // index of the current state buffer\n\n    MeshView view() const {\n        return MeshView{n_owned, nconn, mat, conn, cflux, mat_tc, mat_ext};\n    }\n};\n\ntemplate <typename T>\nT* deviceAlloc(size_t n) {\n    T* p = nullptr;\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&p, std::max<size_t>(n, 1) * sizeof(T)));\n    return p;\n}\n\ntemplate <typename T>\nT* pinnedAlloc(size_t n) {\n    T* p = nullptr;\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaMallocHost(&p, std::max<size_t>(n, 1) * sizeof(T)));\n    return p;\n}\n\ntemplate <typename T>\nvoid toDevice(T* d, const std::vector<T>& h) {\n    if (!h.empty()) CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(d, h.data(), h.size() * sizeof(T), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n}\n\nGpuState setupGpu(const LocalMesh& m) {\n    GpuState g;\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamCreateWithFlags(&g.s_int, cudaStreamNonBlocking));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamCreateWithFlags(&g.s_bnd, cudaStreamNonBlocking));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamCreateWithFlags(&g.s_comm, cudaStreamNonBlocking));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventCreateWithFlags(&g.ev_ghost, cudaEventDisableTiming));\n\n    g.n_owned = m.n_owned;\n    g.n_ghost = m.n_ghost;\n    g.n_send = static_cast<uint32_t>(m.send_local.size());\n    g.n_int = static_cast<uint32_t>(m.interior.size());\n    g.n_bnd = static_cast<uint32_t>(m.boundary.size());\n\n    const size_t n_total = static_cast<size_t>(m.n_owned) + m.n_ghost;\n    const size_t n_own = m.n_owned;\n    const size_t n_slot_entries = static_cast<size_t>(m.n_slots) * n_own;\n    for (int k = 0; k < 2; ++k) {\n        g.E[k] = deviceAlloc<double>(n_total);\n        g.F[k] = deviceAlloc<double>(n_own);\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemset(g.E[k], 0, std::max<size_t>(n_total, 1) * sizeof(double)));\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemset(g.F[k], 0, std::max<size_t>(n_own, 1) * sizeof(double)));\n    }\n\n    g.nconn = deviceAlloc<uint8_t>(n_own);\n    g.mat = deviceAlloc<uint8_t>(n_own);\n    g.conn = deviceAlloc<uint32_t>(n_slot_entries);\n    g.cflux = deviceAlloc<double>(n_slot_entries);\n    g.mat_tc = deviceAlloc<double>(m.mat_tc.size());\n    g.mat_ext = deviceAlloc<double>(m.mat_ext.size());\n    g.interior = deviceAlloc<uint32_t>(m.interior.size());\n    g.boundary = deviceAlloc<uint32_t>(m.boundary.size());\n    g.send_idx = deviceAlloc<uint32_t>(m.send_local.size());\n    g.send_buf = deviceAlloc<double>(m.send_local.size());\n    g.h_send = pinnedAlloc<double>(m.send_local.size());\n    g.h_recv = pinnedAlloc<double>(m.n_ghost);\n\n    toDevice(g.nconn, m.nconn);\n    toDevice(g.mat, m.mat);\n    toDevice(g.conn, m.conn);\n    toDevice(g.cflux, m.cflux);\n    toDevice(g.mat_tc, m.mat_tc);\n    toDevice(g.mat_ext, m.mat_ext);\n    toDevice(g.interior, m.interior);\n    toDevice(g.boundary, m.boundary);\n    toDevice(g.send_idx, m.send_local);\n    return g;\n}\n\nvoid freeGpu(GpuState& g) {\n    for (int k = 0; k < 2; ++k) {\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(g.E[k]));\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(g.F[k]));\n    }\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(g.nconn));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(g.mat));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(g.conn));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(g.cflux));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(g.mat_tc));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(g.mat_ext));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(g.interior));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(g.boundary));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(g.send_idx));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(g.send_buf));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaFreeHost(g.h_send));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaFreeHost(g.h_recv));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventDestroy(g.ev_ghost));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamDestroy(g.s_int));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamDestroy(g.s_bnd));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamDestroy(g.s_comm));\n}\n\ninline unsigned blocksFor(uint32_t n) {\n    return (n + kBlockSize - 1) / kBlockSize;\n}\n\n// Run n_iters update steps. Per step:\n//   1. post halo receives; pack outgoing energies on the GPU and copy them to the host\n//   2. interior update runs on the GPU while the host waits for the packed halo\n//   3. send/receive halo values with neighbouring ranks\n//   4. upload ghost values; boundary update runs once they are on the device\n//   5. join all streams and swap buffers\nvoid runSimulation(const LocalMesh& m, GpuState& g, MPI_Comm comm, int n_iters) {\n    const MeshView view = g.view();\n    std::vector<MPI_Request> reqs(2 * m.nbrs.size());\n\n    for (int iter = 0; iter < n_iters; ++iter) {\n        const int nxt = 1 - g.cur;\n        double* Ec = g.E[g.cur];\n        double* Fc = g.F[g.cur];\n        double* En = g.E[nxt];\n        double* Fn = g.F[nxt];\n\n        int nreq = 0;\n        for (int p : m.nbrs) {\n            if (m.recv_count[p] > 0) {\n                MPI_Irecv(g.h_recv + m.recv_off[p], m.recv_count[p], MPI_DOUBLE, p, kHaloTag, comm,\n                          &reqs[nreq++]);\n            }\n        }\n\n        if (g.n_send > 0) {\n            packKernel<<<blocksFor(g.n_send), kBlockSize, 0, g.s_comm>>>(Ec, g.send_idx, g.send_buf, g.n_send);\n            CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpyAsync(g.h_send, g.send_buf, g.n_send * sizeof(double),\n                                       cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost, g.s_comm));\n        }\n\n        if (g.n_int > 0) {\n            updateKernel<<<blocksFor(g.n_int), kBlockSize, 0, g.s_int>>>(\n                view, g.interior, g.n_int, Ec, Fc, En, Fn);\n        }\n\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(g.s_comm));\n        for (int p : m.nbrs) {\n            if (m.send_count[p] > 0) {\n                MPI_Isend(g.h_send + m.send_off[p], m.send_count[p], MPI_DOUBLE, p, kHaloTag, comm,\n                          &reqs[nreq++]);\n            }\n        }\n        MPI_Waitall(nreq, reqs.data(), MPI_STATUSES_IGNORE);\n\n        if (g.n_ghost > 0) {\n            CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpyAsync(Ec + g.n_owned, g.h_recv, g.n_ghost * sizeof(double),\n                                       cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, g.s_comm));\n        }\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventRecord(g.ev_ghost, g.s_comm));\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamWaitEvent(g.s_bnd, g.ev_ghost, 0));\n\n        if (g.n_bnd > 0) {\n            updateKernel<<<blocksFor(g.n_bnd), kBlockSize, 0, g.s_bnd>>>(\n                view, g.boundary, g.n_bnd, Ec, Fc, En, Fn);\n        }\n\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(g.s_int));\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(g.s_bnd));\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(g.s_comm));\n        g.cur = nxt;\n    }\n}\n\n// Copy this rank's owned final state to the host (OpenMP-parallel unpacking).\nstd::vector<ElementDynamic> downloadOwned(const GpuState& g) {\n    std::vector<double> E(g.n_owned), F(g.n_owned);\n    if (g.n_owned > 0) {\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(E.data(), g.E[g.cur], g.n_owned * sizeof(double), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(F.data(), g.F[g.cur], g.n_owned * sizeof(double), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n    }\n    std::vector<ElementDynamic> out(g.n_owned);\n    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (long long i = 0; i < static_cast<long long>(g.n_owned); ++i) {\n        out[i] = ElementDynamic{E[i], F[i]};\n    }\n    return out;\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Reporting (rank 0, on the gathered global state)\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n// Validate simulation results\nbool validateResults(const std::vector<ElementDynamic>& elements) {\n    val_t energy_sum = 0.0;\n    val_t flux_sum = 0.0;\n    val_t energy_max = std::numeric_limits<val_t>::lowest();\n    val_t energy_min = std::numeric_limits<val_t>::max();\n\n    for (const auto& elem : elements) {\n        energy_sum += elem.current_energy;\n        flux_sum += elem.total_flux;\n        energy_max = std::max(elem.current_energy, energy_max);\n        energy_min = std::min(elem.current_energy, energy_min);\n    }\n\n    printf(\"Validation results:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  Energy sum: %.12f\\n\", energy_sum);\n    printf(\"  Flux sum: %.2f\\n\", flux_sum);\n    printf(\"  Energy range: [%.6f, %.6f]\\n\", energy_min, energy_max);\n\n    // Check for numerical issues\n    constexpr val_t energy_epsilon = 1e-8;\n\n    if (!std::isfinite(energy_sum)) {\n        printf(\"  ERROR: Energy sum is not finite\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    if (std::abs(energy_sum) > energy_epsilon) {\n        printf(\"  WARNING: Energy sum diverged from 0 (expected conservation)\\n\");\n        // Don't fail validation as this can happen with external flows\n    }\n\n    if (!std::isfinite(flux_sum)) {\n        printf(\"  ERROR: Flux sum is not finite\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    if (!std::isfinite(energy_max) || !std::isfinite(energy_min)) {\n        printf(\"  ERROR: Energy extrema are not finite\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    printf(\"  Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n    return true;\n}\n\n// Compute a simple hash of the results for verification\nuint64_t computeHash(const std::vector<ElementDynamic>& elements) {\n    uint64_t hash = 0;\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < elements.size(); ++i) {\n        // Simple hash combining energy and flux values\n        const uint64_t* e_ptr = reinterpret_cast<const uint64_t*>(&elements[i].current_energy);\n        const uint64_t* f_ptr = reinterpret_cast<const uint64_t*>(&elements[i].total_flux);\n        hash ^= (*e_ptr + i) * 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15ULL;\n        hash ^= (*f_ptr + i) * 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9ULL;\n    }\n    return hash;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Grid size (NxN elements) (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -i <num>     Number of simulation iterations (default: 10)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\n}  // namespace\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    int provided = 0;\n    MPI_Init_thread(&argc, &argv, MPI_THREAD_FUNNELED, &provided);\n    int rank = 0;\n    int nranks = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &nranks);\n    const bool root = (rank == 0);\n\n    int n_elems_root = 512;\n    int n_iters = 10;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i
